parity.badSpeed: A speed of {rate}× is not previewed (the preview plays this clip at normal speed); the render applies it.
parity.slow: Slow motion ({rate}×): the preview shows the new timing, but the sound's pitch changes and frames are not blended. The final render is exact.
parity.fast: Fast motion ({rate}×): the preview shows the new timing, but the sound's pitch changes and frames are not blended. The final render is exact.
parity.opticalFlow: Frames are not blended in the preview; the render blends them.
parity.stabilizeFailed: The stabilised preview is not available; the preview shows the unstabilised picture. The export still stabilises the clip.
parity.stabilizeReady: Stabilised preview of the whole source; the export stabilises just this clip's span, so the first and last second can differ slightly.
parity.stabilize: Stabilisation is a two-pass render effect; the preview shows the unstabilised picture.
parity.cornerPin: The corner pin is previewed as a true perspective warp; edges may differ by a pixel.
parity.mask: The shape mask is previewed with the export's soft edge. On a rotated clip the export places it in the turned frame, so it sits in a different spot; with blur or pixelate its edges differ slightly.
parity.reframe: The picture is cropped around the subject to fit the video shape, as in the export; edges may differ by a pixel.
parity.regionEffects: The object is not loaded yet, so the preview shows the clip without its effects; the export applies them.
parity.regionEffectsClose: The effect follows the object's outline from a small copy of the mask; blur and colours are close to the export but not identical.
parity.effects: Some effects are render-only; the preview shows the others.
parity.segmentationApprox: The preview follows a box around the object; the render follows its exact outline.
parity.segmentationOutlineClose: The outline comes from a small copy of the mask, so its edges are close to the export but not identical.
parity.outlinePreparing: Outline preview still preparing, showing a box.
parity.segmentationNoBox: The object mask is not loaded yet, so the preview shows the unmasked picture dimmed; the effect applies in the render.
parity.segmentationUncovered: The object mask does not cover this part of the clip; the render refuses it until the mask covers the whole clip.
parity.effectsApprox: Blur, pixelate, mono and vignette preview on the GPU in the clip's on-canvas geometry at reduced resolution. Rotated clips, softer picture edges and a smaller export differ: the render's blur and pixel size are fixed in output pixels, so a smaller export looks stronger.
parity.lutLoading: A LUT file is still loading; the preview shows the grade without it until it arrives.
parity.lutFailed: The LUT file could not be loaded, so the preview shows the clip without it.
parity.gradeNodesFold: More than 16 corrections: the preview grades the first 16 exactly and folds the rest into one approximate step. Corrections past 16 that use curves, a LUT or a secondary are not shown.
parity.sharpenApprox: Sharpen previews at the render's strength; at a smaller preview size the edge detail is slightly softer.
parity.grainApprox: Film grain previews with the same strength but a different pattern.
parity.primaries: Primaries preview through the GPU with the renderer's formulas; swscale and ffmpeg's own filters round differently.
parity.keyframedTransform: Keyframed transform: the curve is identical, but the preview and the render sample sub-pixel geometry differently.
parity.transformCrop: Transform/crop preview uses GPU bilinear sampling; the render uses swscale.
parity.cutStackGain: Cut, stacking, gain, fades, reverse and hold are previewed as rendered.
parity.titleTemplate: The "{template}" template is previewed with its position, box and border; the text is rasterised by the browser, not by drawtext, so metrics may differ.
parity.titleText: Title text is rasterised by the browser, not by drawtext; metrics may differ.
parity.captionText: Caption text is rasterised by the browser; styling is approximate.
parity.colorGenerator: A colour generator previews as its colour, as rendered.
parity.blendMode: The blend mode is previewed with the render's own formulas; colours can differ by one level where the clip is partly transparent.
parity.barsGenerator: The bars generator draws the render's HD colour bars; the grey ramp's steps can sit a pixel off.
parity.adjustmentApplied: An adjustment clip grades and applies its effects to everything below it, as rendered.
parity.testGenerator: Bars/test generators preview as a flat colour; the render draws the real pattern.
parity.insert: The insert is previewed as a perspective warp; edges may differ by a pixel.
parity.adjustment: An adjustment clip grades the layers below it only in the render.
parity.dissolve: A dissolve is previewed as the same opacity ramp the render applies.
parity.otherTransition: A {type} transition previews as a dissolve; the render applies the real wipe.
parity.xfadeExact: A {type} transition is previewed with the render's own transition maths.
parity.xfadeDissolve: A dissolve transition is previewed with the render's transition maths; the grain pattern differs a little from the render because the GPU computes it slightly differently.
parity.xfadeDistance: A distance transition is previewed with the render's transition maths; the render measures colour distance in YUV and the viewer in RGB, so the edge differs a little.
parity.xfadeFadegrays: A fadegrays transition is previewed with the render's transition maths; the render greys by luma and the viewer by an RGB average, so the grey differs a little.
parity.xfadeHblur: An hblur transition is previewed with the render's transition maths; the viewer samples a very wide blur at 64 points, so the blur is slightly coarser than the render.
parity.compound: A compound clip previews through the flattener (lib/editing/structure/flatten.ts, the renderer's own rules); its contents keep their own parity.
parity.multicam: A multicam clip previews as its angle runs, cut where the render cuts, with the sound from the source chosen for it (the program, one angle, or none).
parity.denoiseLeveler: Denoise and the leveler are not previewed; the render applies them.
parity.busesFallback: These buses cannot be set up in the preview, so the tracks play straight to the master here; the render uses the buses.
parity.dynamicsApprox: Compressor, gate, limiter and de-esser are heard in the preview approximately. Preview is close to the delivered sound; the render is exact.
parity.busesApprox: Bus routing and gain are heard in the preview approximately. Preview is close to the delivered sound; the render is exact.

dsp.compressor: The preview uses the browser compressor: a fixed soft knee, its own attack and release curves (times above one second are capped at one second), and no sidechain filter. Settings are mapped so the loudness change is close; the render is exact.
dsp.limiter: The preview uses a fast compressor and a hard clip at the ceiling, without the render's lookahead, so very fast peaks may sound slightly harsher.
dsp.gate: The preview gate follows the same threshold, ratio, attack and release, but its smoothing curve differs from the render's gate.
dsp.deesser: The preview de-esser turns down a band around 7 kHz when it gets loud. The render uses a different detector, so the amount of reduction is approximate.
dsp.busNote: The buses could not be set up for the preview, so every track plays straight to the master here. The render still uses the buses.
dsp.previewNote: Preview is close to the delivered sound; the render is exact.
